title: Finite projective coordinate reindexing
statement: Let Y and S be schemes and let ι be a finite nonempty coordinate type. If e : Y → ProjectiveSpace ι S is an immersion and e followed by the projection is g : Y → S, then there are n ≥ 0 and an immersion e′ : Y → ProjectiveSpace (ULift (Fin (n+1))) S whose composite with the projection is g.

proof.text: Give ι its finite enumeration and write its positive cardinality as n+1. Compose the enumeration with the universe-lift equivalence. Renaming polynomial variables by this equivalence and its inverse preserves degree and sends the irrelevant ideal onto the irrelevant ideal (both are generated by variables). The two graded maps induce inverse Proj maps by Proj.map_comp and Proj.map_id. Base change these inverse maps along the terminal morphism of S in the definition of relative projective space. The resulting pullback map is an isomorphism and preserves the first projection to S. Compose e with it; the composite is an immersion and its projection is g.

proof_origin.note: Direct proof using polynomial renaming, functoriality of Proj, and base change, checked by R3 second reader.

theorem exists_reindexed_projective_immersion
    {Y S : Scheme.{u}} (ι : Type u) [Finite ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (e : Y ⟶ ProjectiveSpace ι S) [IsImmersion e]
    (g : Y ⟶ S) (h : e ≫ (ProjectiveSpace ι S ↘ S) = g) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (e' : Y ⟶ ProjectiveSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1))) S),
      IsImmersion e' ∧ e' ≫ (ProjectiveSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1))) S ↘ S) = g
